aphoristic.path: Describes sayings that condense an idea into a sharply bounded, memorable form, the same image behind aphorism.

parts.meaning: according to the plumb line, lead

aplomb.path: A plumb line hanging straight and steady under its lead weight became the image of a person standing balanced and composed, hence self-possessed poise under pressure.

apocryphal.path: Religious texts of doubtful authorship were kept 'hidden' outside the accepted canon; the word extended to any widely circulated claim of doubtful truth.

apogee.path: An astronomical term for the point in an orbit farthest from earth, extended to the highest or most distant point of any career or process.

apologist.literal: one who gives a speech in defense
apologist.path: From the formal defense speech (as in Socrates' Apology) to one who habitually defends a doctrine, practice, or institution, often a questionable one.

apostate.path: Literally standing apart from a former position; extended to someone who formally abandons a religion or allegiance.

apostle.path: Named a messenger sent forth to spread a teaching; extended to any early, passionate advocate of a cause.

apothegm.path: Directly, a pointed thing spoken aloud, narrowed to a terse, memorable, instructive saying.

apotheosis.path: The literal deification of a person, elevating them to god status, extended to reaching the highest, most perfect example of something.

apparent.path: Something that shows itself can be either clearly visible and obvious, or merely seeming rather than actually real, and the word carries both senses.

appeal.path: Originally a legal term for driving one's case toward a higher court; extended to making an earnest request, and separately to drawing someone's interest.

appease.path: Bringing a hostile or upset party to peace, often specifically by conceding to their demands.

append.path: Literally hanging one object onto another extended to attaching or adding something at the end of a document or list.

appoint.path: Settling and fixing the details of an arrangement extended to formally assigning a person to a position or office.

apposite.path: Something placed right alongside the matter at hand became the figure for being strikingly appropriate and relevant.

appreciable.path: Originally about assessing the value or price of something, extended to being significant enough in size to be noticed or measured.

apprehension.path: Mentally grasping an idea gave the sense of understanding, while being gripped by a looming worry gave the sense of anxious anticipation.

apprise.path: From mentally grasping or learning a fact to formally passing that knowledge on, i.e. informing someone of it.

approach.path: The literal act of drawing physically near extended to a general method or way of dealing with a matter.

approbation.path: The formal act of testing and proving something sound extended to official or general approval and praise.

approbatory.path: Describes anything that carries or expresses approval, from the same root as approbation.

appropriate.path: Directly, to take something and make it one's own property, often carrying the implication of doing so improperly.

appurtenance.path: Directly names something that belongs to and accompanies a main thing, i.e. an accessory or minor attachment.

appurtenant.path: Describes something that belongs to a main thing as a subordinate part, from the same root as appurtenance.

apropos.path: Directly, being on point and well timed relative to the matter under discussion.

apt.path: Something well fastened to its purpose became the sense of being naturally fitting, or inclined and likely to do something.

aquiline.path: Directly describes a nose curved like the hooked beak of an eagle.

parts.meaning: a witness, one who comes to observe and judge

arbiter.path: Originally a witness called in to observe and give a ruling, directly the ancestor of today's sense: one with the power to settle disputes.

arbitrary.path: Originally meant depending on a judge's personal will rather than fixed law; narrowed to mean based on whim rather than reason.

arbitrate.path: Directly, to act as a neutral arbiter or judge in order to settle a dispute between parties.

arcane.path: Something locked away in a chest and kept secret extended to knowledge understood by only a select few, mysterious to the rest.

arch.path: Used in compounds like 'arch-wag' for a chief joker or mischief-maker; the standalone adjective was later clipped from these to mean knowingly playful or teasing.

archaic.path: Directly describes something belonging to an earlier, ancient period, hence outdated by present standards.

archetype.path: Directly, the original pattern from which copies are made, extended to any typical, representative example of a category.

ardent.path: Literal burning or blazing extended metaphorically to a burning passion and enthusiasm for something.

ardor.path: Names the burning itself: intense passion or enthusiasm, from the same fire image as ardent.

arduous.path: A steep, difficult-to-climb incline became the figure for any task requiring great, uphill effort.

aria.path: Directly names a melodic 'air,' specifically an elaborate solo piece within an opera.

armada.path: Directly, a fleet of armed warships, extended to any large fleet of ships or vehicles.

arrant.path: Applied so often to wandering vagabond thieves ('arrant thief') that it lost its literal sense and became an intensifier meaning utter or complete, always in a bad sense.

arrest.path: Causing something or someone to stop and stand still extended to legal detention and, more generally, to stopping any progress.

arresting.path: Something that literally stops you in your tracks became the figure for being strikingly noticeable, capturing attention.

arriviste.literal: one who has just arrived at shore
arriviste.path: Literally arriving at shore; in French the word shifted to describe an eager social climber who has just 'arrived' at wealth or status, usually with a pushy edge.

arrogate.path: Originally to formally claim something through legal petition, narrowed to seizing or claiming something without proper right.

artful.path: General skillfulness narrowed to a cleverness that can tip into cunning or deceptive craft.

articulate.path: Speech divided into distinct, clearly formed segments, like a jointed structure, became the sense of expressing oneself clearly and effectively.

artifact.path: Directly, something made by human craft; in science, extended to a spurious result produced by the method itself rather than reflecting reality.

artifice.path: Skillful craft narrowed to imply cunning or deceptive craftsmanship, i.e. clever trickery.

artless.path: Directly, lacking artificial craft or contrivance, hence natural, sincere, and without guile.

artlessness.literal: the state of being without artifice
artlessness.path: Names the quality itself behind artless: sincerity and freedom from deceit or affectation.
